title: Emergence and Detection of Surface altermagnetism in KV$_2$Se$_2$O
authors: Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Colin Lange, Sergio Rodriguez, Atasi Chakraborty, Alexander Mook, Jairo Sinov
abstract: We demonstrate the recent concept of emergent surface altermagnetism through its unique signatures in \KVSO. We show that for bulk antiferromagnetically ordered \KVSO, the (001) surface exhibits $d$-wave altermagnetism. Our results fully explain the recent seemingly contradicgting experimental evidence, independently showing both an antiferromagnetically ordered bulk from neutron diffraction, and $d$-wave spin splitting from photoemission spectroscopy. To fully verify this conecept, we predict, as a key experimental signature, a large nonlinear Edelstein response, which is localized at the surface, and follows the $d$-wave altermagnetic symmetry. These results are not only relevant for the metallic and room-temperature magnet \KVSO, but also for several other Lieb lattice systems. Our work expands the pool of techniques that can be used to detect altermagnetism emerging at the surfaces of antiferromagnets.
summary: This work theoretically investigates emergent surface altermagnetism in KV2Se2O by reconciling conflicting experimental data. The authors predict that the unique signature of this phenomenon is a large, symmetry-protected nonlinear Edelstein response localized at the material's surface. They utilize advanced DFT and transport formalisms to calculate these spin responses.
main_problem: The study aims to demonstrate and reconcile the concept of emergent surface altermagnetism in KV2Se2O, explaining conflicting experimental observations regarding bulk antiferromagnetism versus d-wave spin splitting.
main_result: The (001) surface of antiferromagnetically ordered KV2Se2O exhibits d-wave altermagnetism, which is predicted to manifest as a large nonlinear Edelstein response localized at the surface.
method: Theoretical calculations using Density Functional Theory (DFT) combined with advanced techniques like Wannier function renormalization and Boltzmann transport formalism were employed to calculate electronic structure and spin responses.
model_or_system: The physical system is KV2Se2O, a layered material exhibiting Lieb lattice geometry. The analysis models the surface using finite slab calculations, considering different terminations (VO vs SeK).
key_observables: Surface spectral function difference ($\Delta G$), nonlinear Edelstein response ($\chi_{zxx}^{(2)}$), and spin-splitting in electronic band structure.
important_parameters: The analysis is sensitive to surface termination, the number of layers ($N_{	ext{slab}}$), and the magnetic ordering (AM vs AFM).
main_assumptions: Approximations include using a constant relaxation time ($	au$) for transport calculations and relying on DFT/Wannier function methods for electronic structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate surface spectral functions for different magnetic orderings, the slab model setup, and plots showing how the nonlinear Edelstein tensor $\chi^{(2)}$ varies with the number of layers ($N_{	ext{slab}}$) and termination type.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework using DFT/Wannier tools to calculate surface spectral functions. It then applies the Boltzmann formalism to derive symmetry-constrained expressions for linear and nonlinear Edelstein tensors, culminating in predictions for measurable signatures like $\chi^{(2)}$.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the detailed calculation of transport coefficients ($\chi^{(2)}$) using advanced many-body formalisms (Boltzmann equation expansion) provides rigorous theoretical tools applicable to understanding spin-charge coupling phenomena in correlated electron systems.
